name: sol_signature_1
description: Signature replay attack due to missing nonce or chain ID binding
question: The source file in `source` verifies an off-chain-generated signature to authorize an action but the signed data or its validation does not incorporate both a nonce (or other used-signature tracking) and a chain identifier, or does not mark the signature/hash as consumed after use, so a captured valid signature can be replayed on the same chain, another chain, or multiple times to re-execute the authorized action.
criteria: A function recovers a signer from a signature via ecrecover or similar and executes a privileged action without checking or incrementing a per-user or per-message nonce, allowing the same signature to be submitted multiple times
The signed message hash omits block.chainid or an equivalent chain/domain identifier, allowing a signature valid on one chain to be replayed on another chain the contract is deployed to

The contract records that a signature/message hash was used only after performing external calls or state changes, or never marks it as used, so the same signature can be reused before or after invalidation
The signing scheme does not follow EIP-712 domain separation and lacks any nonce or chainid field, making the signed payload replayable across contracts or protocol versions
